source_message.text: With USDC, the approval transaction executed first, but no option to mint appeared afterward. With ETH, there was no approval transaction; the transaction executed and took 0.0140 ETH ($42.60), yet I received no NFT.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
The flow now works as follows:

\- After USDC approval, auto-mint runs, and the success modal appears only once the mint succeeds.
\- For ETH, the price is calculated dynamically, a sufficient buffer is added, and the swap should complete successfully.

To track current market rates, the displayed ETH price will fluctuate against the $30 USDC target. Because the contract minimum is 0.014 ETH (~$43.75), the frontend selects whichever is higher: that minimum or the live dynamic price.

Please hard refresh with Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R, then attempt another mint. Both the USDC and ETH paths should now work correctly.

execution.observed_behavior: The freelancer reports that USDC approval now automatically initiates minting and that the USDC path should work.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I have just deployed to production the fixes for false “Mint Successful” modals and the broken approval-to-mint flow.

The changes are:

\- Modal gating: A success modal now appears only when the mint receipt matches the current mint hash and has not previously been shown. Adding or removing referral codes will not activate it.
\- New-attempt reset: Clicking mint clears the previous success state, pending parameters, and tracking references, preventing stale results from carrying into another attempt.
\- USDC auto-mint: Once approval completes, the USDC mint runs immediately because the stale success guard has been removed; approval by itself can no longer produce success.
\- ETH pricing and buffer: Dynamic ETH pricing still chooses the higher of the live value and the contract minimum of 0.014 ETH, then applies the buffer. This is unchanged from the previous hotfix.

After a hard refresh with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R, please test again:
\- For USDC, approval should automatically initiate the mint, and the modal should wait until the mint transaction confirms.
\- For ETH, a failed transaction should produce no success modal; only an actual mint receipt can trigger one.

If anything else goes wrong, send the latest transaction hashes and I’ll inspect them immediately.

execution.observed_behavior: The freelancer reports deploying a fix that initiates USDC minting immediately after approval and waits for the mint receipt.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Findings

On Base, the ETH mint transaction 0xb842…19e6d reverted. The reason is that the on-chain swap router points to 0x7a91…4c2e rather than the Uniswap V3 SwapRouter. Since the contract sends exactInputSingle to that incorrect address, it reverts; consequently, every ETH mint will continue failing until the router is corrected on-chain.

The USDC mint does work:
\- token #16 exists and belongs to 0x7a14c9e2b6d83f105ac47e69d2b801f43e6c95a1. Its metadata and assets resolve successfully:
\- Metadata: <https://harborquill.example/metadata/1>
\- Image: <https://harborquill.example/images/1.png>

execution.observed_behavior: On-chain inspection confirmed that a USDC mint produced token #16 and assigned it to the buyer's wallet.

The false Purchase Confirmed popup is independently evidence for mint-result feedback, while the approval-without-mint failure is already represented under the USDC flow.
The premature Purchase Confirmed popup should also be evaluated under mint-result feedback.
The Purchase Confirmed modal shown after a reverted USDC attempt is independently a mint-result-feedback failure.

The success modal appearing both before and after the mint transaction concerns mint-result feedback.
The incorrect-router finding and resulting ETH reverts belong to the ETH wallet mint flow.
The success popup shown during USDC approval before minting is a mint-result-feedback failure.
Being stuck on the decrypted book's cover page concerns ebook reader navigation.
The unallocated lottery commission on the no-referral path belongs to no-referral commission allocation.
The weighted-draw ticket-allocation issue belongs to no-referral ticket allocation.
The premature success popup and incorrect token number are mint-result-feedback failures rather than additional USDC execution failures.
